case_name: Jagdish Lal and Others v State of Haryana and Others
facts: The appeal arises from the Division Bench Judgment of Punjab & Haryana High Court, made on November 5, 1996.
The appellants-general candidates challenged the promotion of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe candidates as Superintendents in Class-III Service of Haryana Government.
The reserved candidates were promoted to different posts earlier than the appellants, but the appellants claimed seniority over them for the purpose of promotion to Class-I posts.
issues: Whether the appellants are entitled to be considered for promotion before consideration of the reserved candidates including H.S. Hira as Registrar (Education).
Whether the promotions of the reserved candidates came to be made prior to the decision in Sabharwal's case, and if so, whether they could be declared invalid.
petitioner_arguments: The appellants argued that though the reserved candidates were promoted on different dates as Superintendents etc. earlier to the appellants, they having become members of the Service in the lower cadres earlier to the appellant, were entitled to be considered for further promotion to the higher ladders of the Service.
The appellants claimed seniority over the reserved candidates for the purpose of promotion to Class-I posts.
respondent_arguments: The respondents argued that the reserved candidates became senior to the appellants in the respective cadres by operation of Rule 11 of the Rules, and their promotions are valid in law.
The respondents pointed out that the appellants cannot have any claim to be assigned seniority over and above respondent Nos. 4 to 7 as Superintendents.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the principle laid down in R.K. Sabharwal's case will operate prospectively and not retrospectively.
The Court observed that none of the decisions is of any help for interpreting rules relating to seniority which have been extracted above.
The Court held that seniority will have to be determined in different cadres and categories of posts because the services governed by the Rules of 1974 and 1980 consist of different cadres.
holding: The writ petition deserves to be dismissed on the ground of delay and laches in so far as challenge to the promotion of the respondents as Superintendents/Registrar is concerned.

The principles laid down in Virpal Singh Chauhan's case and Ajit Singh's case will operate prospectively and will not affect promotions of reserved category candidates which were made prior to the decision in R.K. Sabharwal's case or Virpal Singh Chauhan's case.
